title: Bill Pearl Champion Physique Month 5-10
author: Brian T
desc:
This is a continuation of Bill Pearl's 20 month to a Champion Physique program, this follows up from the first published program from month 1-4, within this program it goes from month 5-10 starting at late novice stages and transition into intermediate levels of training. You will notice the volume will go up from now on as you further progress within this program. 

Training is advised to be taken Monday, Wednesday, Friday or Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday. Bill Pearl also recommended to compliment your exercises with at least 20-30 minutes of aerobic exercises as the volume does go up, you do not want your cardiovascular to be the limiting factor.

Bill Pearl had always emphasized that is spelt "train" and not "strain" which means during your sets make sure you have at least 1 or 2 reps left in the tank, if you cannot complete the reps at the rep range without pushing to failure, lower the weight.  Rest in between any set should be from 30 seconds to around 2 minutes.

Bill Pearl (1930 – 2022) is a legendary American bodybuilder who four times won the prestigious title of Mr. Universe (in 1953, 1961, 1967, 1971). Bill Pearl remains one of the most talented bodybuilders who competed prior to the creation of Mr. Olympia contest. He was particularly famous due to his huge arms, ideal muscle proportions and longevity as a bodybuilding athlete, capable of victories at such advanced age as 41.

Born into a poor family and raised performing hard physical work, Bill joined the United States Navy and went to training in Stern’s Gym. There he started his sports career. His main opponents included such outstanding champions as Reg Park, Sergio Oliva, Frank Zane, and later, he was honored with the name “World’s Best-Built Man of the Century.”

Alongside with his competitions, Bill Pearl became a great gym trainer, gym owner, mentor, writer and a good example of vegetarianism.

(For a lot of workouts you see “sit up” as one of the things you should be doing but it’s supposed to be a “bent knee sit up” the diagram shows a bent knee one being done but wanted to clarify hear, bill pearl instructed it to be done on a slight incline of 45 degrees but it doesn’t matter as much if it’s on an incline)
